source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text:
Where the water table is too deep to make pit-digging practical, growers instead build up a planting mound. Bring in about 500g of well-composted topsoil to form a mound roughly matching the size of the potting bag at each planting spot. Carry the seedling to the spot with the bag intact to avoid disturbing the roots; if the bag is a woven/plastic type that will not decompose, carefully cut and remove it rather than planting it with the tree. Space mounds about 1m apart within a row, with roughly 15m between rows. After placing the seedling on top of the mound, add more soil around it and firm gently, then stake and mulch the same way as the pit method.

After either planting method: shade the newly planted seedling for its first weeks (a simple woven-leaf or cloth shade works), water regularly but do not let the base sit in standing water, prune out any damaged or crossing branches, and check for pests and disease symptoms regularly since a young, newly transplanted tree is at its most vulnerable to both.
